A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Group-robust Machine Unlearning, with matching REWEIGHT and MIU methods. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite reorganized presentation and revised experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments on CelebA, Waterbirds and FairFace, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and additional fairness measurements.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on the three image datasets, revised group-prevalence analyses and additional MultiNLI results in Appendix B.4 and Table 16.

M1.justification: REWEIGHT's sampling rule and MIU's unlearning, calibration and retaining objectives remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same alternating procedure after relocation from the appendix. The newly specified estimator architecture documents the existing component; the group classifier introduced in Proposition 1 is part of the derivation, not a new algorithm step.

E1.justification: v2 replaces CelebA attractiveness classification with blond-hair classification, retaining gender as the protected attribute. It also evaluates additional minority and majority populations in the diagnostic experiments and adds MultiNLI, extending coverage beyond the three image datasets.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain L1-sparse, SalUn and SCRUB, alongside the same pretrained and retrained reference models. Retrain + group-DRO was already evaluated in v1; v2 explicitly labels its table rows. MultiNLI uses the existing comparator set rather than introducing another baseline.

E3.justification: The CelebA diagnostic experiment now jointly removes minority and majority groups instead of only attractive males. SalUn's reported tuned subset also changes from 'remaining weights' in v1 Appendix A to 'pruned weights' in v2 Section 4.1; this establishes a documentation-level protocol revision, not that experiments were rerun. Shared image-experiment budgets, backbone and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 2 and 7 substantially expand the degradation analysis into explicit minority-versus-majority comparisons across all three image datasets, testing how group prevalence affects vulnerability to unlearning. Component ablations, lambda sensitivity, multi-group FairFace experiments and additional fairness analyses already existed in v1; these are retained, with revised CelebA results.

E5.justification: Both versions report deltas averaged over three runs, appendix standard deviations and three-seed lambda experiments. v2's additional result rows follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no increased run count, confidence interval or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: CelebA results are extensively replaced following the task change: Table 1's MIU + REWEIGHT GA changes from 69.0 to 41.3 and average gap from 99.2 to 99.0, which are not same-setting performance changes. New MultiNLI results report average gaps of 96.0 for MIU + REWEIGHT, 95.9 for SalUn + REWEIGHT and 92.5 for SCRUB + REWEIGHT. Most existing Waterbirds and FairFace table values are retained.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.4 introduces Proposition 1 and an entropy/KL-divergence derivation claiming equivalence between mutual-information minimization and cross-entropy maximization on a group classifier. v1 contains the estimator and loss equations but no corresponding proposition or proof. This adds substantive theoretical justification without changing the method.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion qualify degradation as something that 'can' occur, consistent with the new evidence that majority groups can be less affected. The principal contributions—identifying group-robust unlearning, proposing REWEIGHT and MIU, and outperforming established baselines—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 refines the explanation of degradation around minority groups' shrinking representation and majority groups' relative resilience. It adds a concrete group-discovery suggestion for addressing unavailable annotations and changes the stated evaluation boundary from image classification to classification. Most existing explanations of reweighting, overfitting and privacy–utility tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies that the mutual-information estimator is a two-layer ReLU MLP producing one scalar and explicitly identifies the five-sample Waterbirds forget set at ratio 0.1. Most hardware, optimization, timing and pseudocode details were already in v1's appendix, and the code-link destination is unchanged. The added MultiNLI experiment lacks a specified model and group definition.

R1.justification: v2 adds Boudiaf et al. (2020) for the new derivation and Williams et al. (2018) for MultiNLI. It explicitly distinguishes REWEIGHT from Idrissi et al.'s uniform-group reweighting and positions group-robust unlearning as a generalization of random unlearning without the i.i.d. assumption. The broader related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: The document substantially reorganizes existing material: implementation details, Algorithm 1 and the GA definition move into the main paper, while limitations and societal impacts move alongside the conclusion. Appendices A–D become A–B. Terminology changes from 'retain' to 'remaining', with additional paragraph revisions and journal-style author and citation formatting.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column presentation with a predominantly single-column journal layout and extensively relocates displays. Figure 1 is rearranged horizontally, Figure 2 gains a second panel, Figure 7 expands from three to six panels, and a MultiNLI table is added. Table captions move above tables and group-DRO row labels become explicit.

improvement.justification: v2 adds informative minority/majority comparisons and broader empirical coverage, but MultiNLI lacks essential model and group details. The new Proposition 1 does not establish why its KL term can be disregarded when encoder updates change the features. Revised CelebA ablations also disagree between Tables 4 and 17 on UA without the retaining term: 27.2 versus 27.8. These evidential gains and newly introduced reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
